children: Wednesday it signed a multi-year agreement with Amazon
covering custom chips used in Amazon's cloud computing business.
The agreement, valued at more than $1B, expands Amazon's use of Synopsys' chip-design technology and related software. The companies have worked together for more than 15 years.

Amazon has developed its own chips for cloud security, networking, storage, and artificial intelligence, including its Graviton and Trainium processors. Under the new agreement, Amazon will also use Synopsys' application-specific chip technology and other design and simulation tools.
The companies said they will also work on using artificial intelligence in the process of designing and testing chips and computer systems.
Synopsys will use Amazon's cloud computing services to develop its own chip-design products. It will also use Amazon Bedrock, a service for building AI applications, to develop AI tools.

"Special purpose silicon is at the heart of AWS innovation. As we expand into application-optimized IP solutions, we're proud to have Amazon as our lead customer for this next phase of growth,” said Synopsys CEO Sassine Ghazi.

"Amazon has invested in custom silicon for more than a decade, and it has fundamentally changed what’s possible for AWS and our customers,” said Peter DeSantis, SVP, foundational AI, custom silicon, quantum computing at Amazon. “From Graviton to Trainium, purpose-built chips deliver better performance at lower cost because they’re designed for exactly what customers need. As our chip designs grow more ambitious and AI reshapes the engineering process itself, Synopsys helps us move faster across the design cycle, helping us deliver more capable, efficient computing for customers worldwide.”

title: Synopsys, Amazon sign multiyear agreement for custom chips
